name: W bialgebra
summary: A W merge followed by a W split equals W splits followed by W merges, with a fermionic crossing.
description:
The W-node (black triangle) with one input and $n$ outputs maps $|0\rangle \mapsto |0\cdots 0\rangle$ and $|1\rangle \mapsto |10\cdots0\rangle + |010\cdots0\rangle + \cdots + |0\cdots01\rangle$: it spreads a single excitation over its outputs in all possible ways. The small dot marks its input leg.

The W-node read as a merge (dot on the right) and as a split (dot on the left) form a bialgebra, but only up to a sign: the two wires that cross must be connected by Hadzihasanovic's *crossing*, the 'fermionic swap' $|00\rangle\langle00| + |01\rangle\langle10| + |10\rangle\langle01| - |11\rangle\langle11|$, which picks up a sign when both wires carry an excitation. With an ordinary swap the rule is false. PyZX has no crossing generator, so here it is written as a swap followed by a CZ gate (two Z-spiders joined by a Hadamard edge).

This is axiom 5a of Hadzihasanovic's ZW-calculus (black monoid and comonoid form a Hopf algebra), generalised to $\mathrm{ba}_W^{n,m}$. Its companion with a Z-spider, the [W/Z bialgebra](../w-z-bialgebra/), needs no crossing.
parameter_notes: Shown for two inputs and two outputs; holds for any numbers of inputs and outputs, with a fermionic crossing between every pair of crossing wires.

also_in.location: Section 3 (The rules), generalised bialgebra rule I, $\mathrm{ba}_W^{n,m}$
Chapter 5, Section 5.2 (list of rules of the ZW calculus), rule $ba_w$

notes: The crossing of the ZW-calculus is not a generator in PyZX; it is represented here by a swap and a CZ (Hadamard edge between two phase-free Z-spiders), which has the same linear map. The scalar $\sqrt{2}$ compensates for the normalisation of the Hadamard edge: the Z-spiders joined by a Hadamard edge are $\mathrm{CZ}/\sqrt{2}$.
